answer: Each agent must lock a scarce stake before its claims can earn reputation, and a randomly selected set of independent validators checks the work before rewards are released. Splitting one identity into a hundred does not multiply the stake’s influence: each claim still needs costly backing, and dishonest claims can forfeit it. An attacker must therefore buy and risk real capital for every fake identity, while honest agents can reuse a verified history. A dune, quill, or fable may be cheap; persistent economic weight is not.
